# HeatEquationKernel demo

A small waLBerla application that solves the 2D transient heat equation with a
**temperature-dependent thermal diffusivity** generated by MaterForge from a
single declarative YAML file (`1.4301_HeatEquationKernelWithMaterial.yaml`,
stainless steel 1.4301 / AISI 304).

It is the minimal end-to-end example of the MaterForge → pystencils/sweepgen →
waLBerla code-generation path:

- `create_material(...)` builds symbolic property expressions from the YAML
  (tabular `.xlsx` imports, piecewise equations, and computed properties);
- the discretized PDE substitutes `thermal_diffusivity(u)` into the generated
  sweep, so the kernel sees the material's temperature dependence directly;
- `material.compile()` (the v0.9.0 fast evaluator) and the on-disk build cache
  (v0.9.1) are exercised so repeated code-generation runs stay cheap;
- `PiecewiseInverter` demonstrates the energy-density → temperature inversion
  with a round-trip accuracy check.

> **Build system:** built through the top-level
> [`apps/CMakeLists.txt`](../CMakeLists.txt) driver. Configure from `apps/`; the
> binary lands in `apps/build/<preset>/`. See [`apps/README.md`](../README.md)
> for prerequisites.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `CodegenHeatEquationWithMaterial.cpp` | waLBerla driver that runs the generated sweep |
| `HeatEquationKernelWithMaterial.py`   | pystencils/sweepgen code generator + MaterForge integration |
| `1.4301_HeatEquationKernelWithMaterial.yaml` | MaterForge material spec |
| `1.4301_HeatEquationKernelWithMaterial.xlsx` | tabular property data referenced by the YAML |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | app target (driven by the top-level `apps/` build) |

## Build & run

```bash
cd apps/

# Configure + build (CPU). Use -DBUILD_COUETTE_FLOW=OFF to build only this app.
cmake --preset local-release-cpu -DBUILD_COUETTE_FLOW=OFF
cmake --build --preset local-release-cpu-build

# Run the generated executable
./build/local-release-cpu/HeatEquationKernel/HeatEquationWithMaterial
```

Inspecting the material from the command line:

```bash
materforge info apps/HeatEquationKernel/1.4301_HeatEquationKernelWithMaterial.yaml
```
